Squats for strengthening your legs and lower back; allows you to pick up heavy stuff and/or carry it on your back. It also strengthens many smaller muscles that otherwise don't get much attention, which help with regular movements, like walking and running.

Deadlifts for strengthening your hamstrings, lower back, and forearms/hands; allows you to pick up heavy stuff and also run better (hamstrings are important for running and also walking).

Pull-ups for strengthening your shoulders, arms, and upper back; allows you to pull yourself up and do other stuff with your arms.

Barbell rows for strengthening your back, arms, and balancing muscles; allows you to pull stuff up, balance better, and generally supports a number of muscles that you might use in a given movement.

Bench press or similar variation for strengthening your chest, shoulders, and arms; allows you to push stuff.

(this is basically Stronglifts 5x5)

Running for cardiovascular strength and endurance; allows you to do stuff for longer using less energy.

Warming up and warming down, plus stretching, are always a good idea. Nothing promotes injury more than muscles and connective tissue that are "cold".
